data.why: The app's /draw route always calls mutalyzer.fetch_exons(), which performs a live HTTPS lookup to mutalyzer.nl; the sandbox has no network at runtime, so the patched mutalyzer.py replaces that lookup with a small offline cache (keyed by the variant-free transcript string) covering every example shown in the web form's own instructions table, so the full view/variant/crop/export workflow can run without the network.

goals: Visualize a transcript's exon structure as a scaled SVG diagram, starting from a gene name, a transcript accession, or an HGVS variant description
Check which exon(s) a variant falls in and see it marked on the diagram
See reading frames and coding/non-coding exon boundaries highlighted across exons
Restrict the diagram to a specific range of exons (first/last exon)
Download the rendered diagram as an SVG file
Adjust display options (exon color, variant colors, scale, exon height/width/gap, exon numbering, variant marker shape) and see the effect on the diagram

review.summary: The tree describes ExonViz accurately as a tool for drawing transcripts to scale and marking variants. Its phases, tasks and five features are sensible, and nearly all cited screens show what their nodes claim. It needs a fix before filing: one screen (020) doesn't show its claimed download, the reading-frame reading the README emphasises has no task, and a few of the agent's own test actions should be moved out of the user's tasks.
